decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit (ACE3) sits at the core of the firm's airfield lighting expertise, where its deep related knowledge and own R&D let it interpret field results and keep improving the product.

The air situation display builds on the firm's tower and surveillance integration know-how and complements its integrated offer, so it can still absorb feedback and refine it, although it is less central than lighting.
The airport systems training program draws directly on the firm's long operational experience, costs little to sustain, and generates customer learning that feeds back into its service business.
The airfield ground lighting training course extends the firm's strongest knowledge domain and supports its installed base, so it fits well with the existing business and is cheap to keep.

The collaboration software tool matches the firm's strategic move toward data-driven collaborative decision-making, and its systems-integration capability lets it learn from deployments, though software iterations may replace it.

The multilateration surveillance system broadens the firm's surveillance portfolio, and its R&D and integration capabilities give enough related knowledge to develop it, despite more competitive and less familiar technology.
